name: Stockton Economic Empowerment Demonstration
executionNotes: The household-benefit model can estimate reach and cost but does not model employment; a randomized treatment/control employment adapter is required.
forecastQuestion: Before payments began, how would one year of unconditional $500 monthly transfers affect full-time employment among recipients relative to controls?
summary: Forecast first-year employment response to an unconditional $500 monthly transfer in a randomized city pilot.

sources.title: SEED employment findings
sources.locator: First-year employment findings: treatment 28% to 40%; control 32% to 37%

confounds: The treatment group contained only 125 recipients.
The first-year window ends as the COVID-19 pandemic begins.
Pilot estimates should not be extrapolated directly to a citywide permanent program.
evaluationDesign: Randomized controlled pilot with treatment and control outcomes; external-validity stress test.

verification.method: Every source URL was fetched and compared against the document it claims to be, and every scored figure was looked for in the source it cites.
findings: Both employment figures are verbatim on the SEED findings page: recipients 28 percent to 40 percent full-time over the year, control 32 percent to 37 percent. The design (125 residents, $500 a month, 24 months) matches the locator word for word.
